_fieldSizeSource: WPILib AprilTagField.k2026RebuiltWelded via robotpy-apriltag 2026.2.2. NOT the 54x27 ft figure quoted in general sources -- that gives 16.4592 x 8.2296 and an aspect of 2.0000, where the authoritative layout is 2.0499. The width differs by 2%, which is enough to matter.
_method: The horizontal rails are thin (17-20 px) and unambiguous, so the y bounds are taken from their centres: 86.0 and 1496.0, giving 1410 px for 8.0690 m = 174.74 px/m. The x bounds follow from that scale, centred on the detected centre line (x=1949.5). Both implied x edges land INSIDE the 67 px-thick alliance-wall structures at 457-523 and 3376-3442, which is consistent -- the wall has thickness and the field boundary lies within it.
_warning: An earlier version of this file FORCED width = 2 x height from a 54x27 ft assumption, then 'verified' that the implied edges landed near structures. That verification was circular and the result was wrong. Do not re-derive this from a nominal field size; use the WPILib layout.
_displayOnly: This mapping is for RENDERING onto the field image. It is an illustration and is not guaranteed metrically exact. Metric truth for robot positions comes from the AprilTag-derived camera pose (data/field/2026-apriltag-layout.json), which is in true WPILib metres. Any inaccuracy here affects where a dot is drawn, never the recorded position.
convention: WPILib 2026: origin at the field corner, +x along the 16.5410 m axis, +y along the 8.0690 m axis, z up. Image +x maps to field +x; image +y maps to field -y (image rows increase downward).
